approvalText: Approve all five ME-6 relationships, their identified PMIDs/DOIs, and the proposition-specific publication guards from the successfully revalidated discovery ledger for local-only, fail-closed implementation against baseline 3e47fae71adf4ab80e7804076c36e2c839790e17; all five new sources enter verified:false / pending-verification, with no citation promotion, semantic broadening, taxonomy change, or remote writes.

rows.citation: Monticone S, D'Ascenzo F, Moretti C, et al. Cardiovascular events and target organ damage in primary aldosteronism compared with essential hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. 2018;6(1):41-50. PMID 29129575. doi:10.1016/S2213-8587(17)30319-4.
rows.publicationGuard: Use the broad cardiac-arrhythmia target only for separately documented atrial fibrillation. Require a confirmed primary-aldosteronism phenotype with autonomous aldosterone excess and suppressed renin; do not generalize this source to unspecified hyperaldosteronism. Treat the meta-analysis as population-level excess-risk evidence, not proof that primary aldosteronism caused atrial fibrillation in an individual. Preserve age, hypertension duration and severity, structural or valvular heart disease, thyroid disease, sleep-disordered breathing, alcohol exposure, and other established atrial-fibrillation contributors.

rows.citation: Bandak M, Lauritsen J, Johansen C, et al. Sexual Function in a Nationwide Cohort of 2,260 Survivors of Testicular Cancer after 17 Years of Followup. J Urol. 2018;200(4):794-800. PMID 29730199. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2018.04.077.
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented testicular cancer, actual exposure to a treatment regimen supported by the source (including BEP chemotherapy, abdominal radiotherapy, post-chemotherapy retroperitoneal surgery, or multiple treatment lines as applicable), and separately established erectile dysfunction with compatible post-treatment chronology. Do not infer erectile dysfunction from the cancer diagnosis or unilateral orchiectomy alone. Preserve pre-treatment erectile symptoms, hypogonadism, vascular and metabolic disease, medications, neurologic disease, psychological or relationship factors, and other erectile-dysfunction causes.

rows.citation: Ki EY, Park JS, Lee KH, Hur SY. Incidence and Risk Factors of Lower Extremity Lymphedema After Gynecologic Surgery in Ovarian Cancer. Int J Gynecol Cancer. 2016;26(7):1327-1332. PMID 27400319. doi:10.1097/IGC.0000000000000757.
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented ovarian cancer, documented pelvic and/or para-aortic lymph-node dissection or lymphadenectomy, and separately established lower-extremity lymphedema with compatible postoperative chronology. Do not infer lymphedema from ovarian cancer, chemotherapy, or pelvic surgery without lymphatic-node disruption alone. Preserve venous thrombosis or insufficiency, obesity, infection, cardiac or renal edema, prior pelvic surgery or radiotherapy, malignant obstruction, and other causes of lower-extremity swelling.

rows.phenotypeRestriction: advanced chronic liver disease with portal hypertension
rows.citation: Scheiner B, Semmler G, Maurer F, et al. Prevalence of and risk factors for anaemia in patients with advanced chronic liver disease. Liver Int. 2020;40(1):194-204. PMID 31444993. doi:10.1111/liv.14229.
rows.publicationGuard: Restrict this source proposition to documented advanced chronic liver disease with clinically established portal-hypertension or comparable advanced-disease features and require separately established anemia. Treat the source as population-level prevalence and risk-factor evidence, not proof that chronic liver disease caused anemia in an individual. Preserve gastrointestinal bleeding, iron or other nutritional deficiency, hemolysis, hypersplenism, chronic kidney disease, marrow disease, malignancy, medications or treatment effects, and other anemia etiologies.

rows.citation: Köhler JR, Tencer J, Thysell H, et al. Long-term effects of reflux nephropathy on blood pressure and renal function in adults. Nephron Clin Pract. 2003;93(1):C35-C46. PMID 12411757. doi:10.1159/000066639.
rows.publicationGuard: Restrict this proposition to chronic pyelonephritis with objectively documented reflux-nephropathy or pyelonephritic renal scarring and require separately established hypertension. Do not generalize reflux-nephropathy evidence to a remote history of acute pyelonephritis or recurrent urinary infection without chronic renal damage. Treat the cohort as phenotype-specific risk evidence, not automatic individual causation. Preserve primary hypertension, diabetes, chronic kidney disease from other causes, renal-artery disease, endocrine causes, medications, and other contributors.
